title: Debounce transient edit previews to avoid duplicate token credits in interactive compose flows
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: In interactive editing/compose flows (e.g., reply composer, collaborative doc previews, rapid A/B prompt edits), clients often issue a sequence of short requests and preview renders. Each request can incur input+output token billing immediately when processed by the inference runtime. This leads to inflated charges for customers and poor UX when previews are used heavily. We have multiple customer reports of unexpectedly high bills after prolonged preview usage.

This ticket proposes a server-side debounce/provisional-credit mechanism that avoids finalizing billing for transient preview requests until a short idle/finalize heuristic is satisfied. The approach aims to preserve correctness of accounting while reducing duplicate charges for edits that are quickly superseded. It must be compatible with streaming responses, not introduce unbounded state, and provide robust observability and fail-open behavior so that traffic is never dropped or charged incorrectly under system pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Server maintains provisional token credits per session/request id and only converts provisional credits to final charges when a finalize signal or idle window expiration occurs
Feature is behind an org-level feature flag and can be enabled for a subset of tenants
No increase in tail latency >3% for preview flows when feature is enabled (measured p99 request-to-first-byte)
Unit/integration/bench tests simulate 10k concurrent preview-edit sessions with <5% memory overhead over baseline
Billing audit logs clearly show provisional -> finalized transition events and are queryable per-customer
design_notes: Core idea: introduce a short-lived provisional-credit stage in the metering pipeline. When a request arrives marked as 'preview' (client header or inferred), we allocate provisional input+output token credits but do not emit final billing events until conversion.
Conversion triggers: explicit client finalize signal (preferred), detection of session idle > default_window (15s), or periodic flush when provisional count per-session exceeds safety cap.

For streaming responses we emit provisional output chunks immediately to downstream clients (to avoid UX regression) but tag those chunks with provisional token markers. Finalization will convert provisional markers to final charges; if a preview is superseded, provisional credits are expired and not converted.
Fallbacks: under high-memory or queue pressure, system will fall back to immediate billing (feature flag exposes 'fail-open' behavior). All fallbacks must be recorded in logs for reconciliation.

Idempotency: require clients to send request idempotency key. If absent, server generates one and returns it so follow-up edits can reference the same editing session for dedupe. This is necessary to reconcile rapid re-sends from flaky clients.

Safety caps: per-session provisional cap (default 4k tokens) and global provisional budget per customer to avoid abuse. Exceeding caps triggers immediate conversion to final charges and an alert to the customer's org admin if enabled.
tasks: API: extend request schema/headers to accept X-Redwood-Preview and X-Redwood-Finalize or client-provided session-id
Metering: add provisional-credit store TTL-managed (redis) and conversion logic in billing pipeline
Streaming: annotate stream frames with provisional markers and ensure client SDK maps markers to local preview state
UI/SDK: update JS SDK to expose finalize() call and automatic session-id attachment for compose flows
Feature flag: add org-level gate and rollout config with rollout percent and memory-pressure disable
Tests: unit, integration, load simulations and end-to-end billing reconciliation tests
Dashboard: Grafana panels for provisional_credit_ratio, conversion_latency, provisional_memory_usage
Doc: internal runbook for refunds and an external docs note describing preview billing semantics
test_plan: Unit tests for conversion logic, provisional TTL expiry, and idempotency behavior
Integration test: preview -> finalize flow across streaming+non-streaming models; verify billing events in test billing DB
Load test: 10k concurrent preview sessions for 10 minutes in staging; track memory and conversion latency
Reconciliation test: inject dropped finalize signal and verify TTL expiry correctly expires provisional credits without producing charges
monitoring: metric: provisional_conversion_latency (time from provisional allocation to finalization)
alert: conversion_latency_p95 > 30s for 5m => severity P1; investigate queue/backpressure
alert: provisional_memory_usage > 70% of allowed budget for any region => auto-disable feature flag for affected orgs
comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha Menon: Initial draft. Added acceptance criteria and proposed 15s idle window. Requesting PM/design input on UX finalize signal.

2026-02-25 - Mei Chen (Design): UX OK with preview header approach; prefers explicit finalize for keyboard 'send' and auto-finalize on blur after timeout. Raised accessibility concern for autosave flows.

2026-03-03 - Ravi Patel (PM): Prioritize for mid-market customers who reported billing spikes. Suggested feature-flagged rollout and telemetry to compute estimated customer savings; set target to reduce preview-related overcharges by 60% in pilot orgs.

2026-03-07 - Anil Gupta (Reliability): Reviewed memory/capacity implications. Recommends Redis hash TTL with LRU eviction and global provisional budget per region. Asked for a fail-open switch to avoid increasing p99 latency under pressure.
2026-03-10 - Diego Ruiz: Implementing provisional store prototype. PRs created for runtime and metering. Coordinating with billing team on finalization events and refund path for legacy customers.

2026-03-12 - Laura Kim (Billing): Noted that refunds for converted provisional credits are complex; recommends we avoid retroactive refunds and instead only prevent conversion. Billing will accept finalized events as canonical.
decision_log: 2026-02-28: Chosen default idle window = 15s (tradeoff: shorter window reduces delay but increases duplicate billing risk).
2026-03-04: Use provisional credits that are never billed until converted; no retroactive negative invoices allowed. Billing team to treat conversion events as authoritative.
2026-03-06: Feature will be org-gated with rollout percent and will auto-disable under memory pressure.
notes_for_release: Expose preview billing semantics in customer-facing docs and console billing tab during pilot
Provide a short migration guide for SDK users showing how to call finalize() and attach session ids
Telemetry: ensure invoiceable token counts in Billing DB are only written after conversion events
